question.value: Does the Class 0 protostar HH 212 host a rotationally supported disk inside an infalling flattened envelope (pseudodisk), and what are the properties of the HCO+ jet?

evidence.quote: In order to confirm the presence of a RSD in this system, we have mapped this system in 350 GHz continuum and HCO$^+$ J=4-3 using Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA) at higher resolution and sensitivity.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00647.S.
Two scheduling blocks (SBs) were obtained in Band 7 at $\sim$ 350 GHz with 21-24 antennas

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 spectral windows (CO 3-2, SiO 8-7, HCO+ 4-3, continuum); ~0.2 km/s channels for the line windows; 9-pointing mosaic

evidence.quote: The correlator was set up to have 4 spectral windows, with one for CO J=3-2, one for SiO J=8-7, one for HCO$^+$ J=4-3, and one for the continuum.
A 9-pointing mosaic was used to observe the jet in this system within $\sim$ $35''$ from the central source.
We have mapped it in 350 GHz continuum and HCO$^+$ J=4-3 emission with ALMA

findings_qualitative.value: The flattened envelope is infalling with small rotation and is identified as a pseudodisk; an extended infalling envelope flowing roughly parallel to the jet axis is needed to explain the missing low-redshifted HCO+ emission.

evidence.quote: an extended infalling envelope is required, with its material flowing roughly parallel to the jet axis toward the pseudodisk.

claims.hypothesis: The flattened envelope is a pseudodisk with infall and small rotation.
claims.experiment: HCO+ spectrum, channel maps and PV diagrams
claims.result: Blue-brighter double peak with redshifted dip and triangular PV structure
claims.finding: Envelope is infalling and spiraling; identified as a pseudodisk

evidence.quote: The HCO$^+$ kinematics shows that the flattened envelope is infalling with small rotation (i.e., spiraling) into the central source

claims.hypothesis: A rotationally supported disk exists at the center.
claims.experiment: Continuum CLEAN map and HCO+ kinematics at high velocity, plus modeling
claims.result: Compact disk radius ~120 AU with Keplerian-like rotation; Keplerian radius equals model disk radius
claims.finding: Disk is rotating and can be rotationally supported, though it is unresolved and Keplerian rotation needs confirmation

evidence.quote: However, further observations at higher resolution are needed to confirm its Keplerian rotation and its radius.

claims.hypothesis: A density jump exists at the envelope-disk interface.
claims.result: m ~ 8, consistent with an isothermal shock with Mach number ~2.82
claims.finding: A density jump is required to match disk continuum emission

evidence.quote: a jump in density with a factor of $\sim$ 8 is required across the interface between the flattened envelope and the disk.

claims.hypothesis: The HCO+ jet traces internal shocks.
claims.experiment: Jet map and PV diagram for |Voff|>=2 km/s, abundance estimate
claims.result: Peaks upstream of SiO, velocity range ~14 km/s, abundance ~1e-7
claims.finding: HCO+ traces internal shocks in the jet with enhanced abundance

evidence.quote: The broad velocity range and high HCO$^+$ abundance indicate that the HCO$^+$ emission traces internal shocks in the jet.

limitations_admitted.value: Disk is not well resolved, so its radius is an upper limit and the temperature index is rough; model is simple and symmetric and excludes outflow, jet and extended envelope.

evidence.loc: 4 Model of the envelope and disk
evidence.quote: The disk is not well resolved in our observations, especially in the minor axis.

evidence.loc: 4 Model of the envelope and disk
evidence.quote: Our model here is simple and can be considered as a first step to disentangle the envelope and disk in our system.

referee_caveats_inferred: Model fit is by eye with no uncertainties or parameter degeneracies quantified
Disk is unresolved, so the Keplerian and density-jump conclusions rest on model assumptions
Extended envelope treated ad hoc with a Gaussian
Fixed assumptions (beta=1, Tex=50 K, 20% mass-loss fraction) drive the abundance
